facility.name: The Academy at Craig Ranch
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Before School Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver dropped a nicotine pouch in the childcare area and a child later put this nicotine pouch into their mouth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: A child was able to pick up and put in their mouth a nicotine pouch that had been left out on the floor of a childcare area at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information-Child's allergies and Completed Food Allergy Plan: Two children with diagnosis food allergies did not have a complete F.A.R.E./emergency allergy plan from a health care professional on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information-Child's allergies and Completed Food Allergy Plan (26 TAC §746.605(15))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Annual Sanitation Inspection: The operation does not have a current annual sanitation/health inspection.  Last inspection is noted April 2025.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3403)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Enrollment Agreement: A child file did not have acknowledgement from a parent validating that the center's operational policies were received and/or obtained.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Enrollment Agreement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: A child's admission information did not list a parent signature for authorization for emergency medical treatment in the event of a parent cannot be reached to arrange for emergency medical care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Physician Information (26 TAC §746.605(11))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: A caregiver did not wash an child's hands after a diaper change.  The deficiency was corrected during the inspection when it was brought to the caregivers attention to washed the child's hands with soap and running water to help prevent the spread of germs.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child: A caregiver did not wash their hands with soap and running water after changing a child's diaper.  The deficiency was corrected during the inspection when it was brought to the caregivers attention to wash their hands to prevent the spread of germs when transition to changing other child's diaper or working with a groupn of children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child (26 TAC §746.3415(4))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities: A group of young children did not wash their hands after returning to the classroom after outdoor play but instead the children transition to circle time.  The caregivers corrected the deficiency during the inspection when it was brought to their attention to wash the children hands with soap and running water after outdoor play.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities (26 TAC §746.3417(4))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required: A caregiver is lacking 22 annual training hours from 5/5/2025 to 5/5/2026.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Safety Documentation for Emergency Drills, Fire Extinguishers, & Smoke Detectors: The a record of the emergency practices such as fire, weather, lockdown drills, fire extiguisher checks, CO and smoke detector test were not available.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Safety Documentation for Emergency Drills, Fire Extinguishers, & Smoke Detectors (26 TAC §746.801(10))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - School Information for School-age Child: Two children that attend public school did not have name and contact number of the public school.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Special Needs Statement (26 TAC §746.605(13))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: Two caregivers with a pending background check was observed working in a classroom with a group of children. The deficiency was corrected during inspection when the caregivers left the building.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: A child's file did not a persons name, address, and phone of who to reach when the parent is not available during an emergency.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: It was determined that the that a two-year-old left the classroom and the caregivers present were not aware of it.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended: It was determined during the investigation that a child was left unattended and alone on the bus.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended (26 TAC §746.5605(4))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: It was determined in the investigation that the operation director did not have transportation training completed that was up to date and not expired.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: During the investigation it was determined that a caregiver grabbed and pulled a child due to the child's behavior.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During the investigation it was determined that a caregiver did not demonstrate competency and self-control with a child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on the interviews with the staff and the parent of the victim, a caregiver did not adequately supervise a young child which resulted in a young child finger being smash in the corner of a restroom door.  The young child received an amputation fracture on their right ring finger.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required: A caregiver lacks 19 clock hours of annual training from April 18, 2024 to April 14, 2025.  A caregiver lacks 21 clock hours of annual training from August 6, 2024 to August 6, 2025.  A caregiver is lacks 21 clock hours of annual training from October 14, 2023 to October 14, 2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Communicable Diseases: A young child/victim did not have a written incident report on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Communicable Diseases (26 TAC §746.701(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on interviews with the staff and a parent, a young child was not adequately supervised which resulted in a young child taking another young child's bottle during a feeding a proceeded to drink the young child formula.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: Based on the interviews with staff, the management did not have a written incident report of a situation the placed a child at risk.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on interviews with staff and other collaterals, and a video, the operation was not in compliance with the standard evaluated.  A young child was left alone in a classroom unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on the interview with the parent and staff, a caregiver did not use good judgement when the caregiver bottle feed an infant another infant's bottle of breast milk and formula.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Bottles & Training Cups Labeled for Each Toddler: An infant bottle was not labeled with the child's first name and the initial of the child's last name.  An infant's baby food was not labeled with the infant's first name and the initial of the infant's last name.  The deficiency was corrected during the inspection when the caregiver wrote the infants' first names and the initials of the infants' last name on the bottle and the baby food.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Bottles & Training Cups Labeled for Each Toddler (26 TAC §746.2505(4)(A))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on interviews with the parent and management, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the minimum standards for a licensed childcare center. Management reported a situation that placed a child at risk more than two days after the incident occurred.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information-Child's allergies and Completed Food Allergy Plan: Based on observations and the interview with the parent, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the minimum standard for a licensed childcare center.   The operation did not have a complete food allergy plan on file for a child with a diagnosis food allergy.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information-Child's allergies and Completed Food Allergy Plan (26 TAC §746.605(15))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child: Based on the interview with caregiver, the victim, and the parent, the operation served a child in care food identified on their allergy emergency plan.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child (26 TAC §746.3301(i))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on interviews with staff and the parent, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the minimum standards for licensed childcare centers.  A child was left alone unsupervised in an indoor play area.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Gas Leak Inspection: The current gas leak inspection was not available.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Gas Leak Inspection (26 TAC §746.5405)

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Gas Leak Inspection: The current gas leak inspection was not available.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Gas Leak Inspection (26 TAC §746.5405)

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Steps- Prompt: Based on interviews with parents and staff, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the standard evaluated.  Caregivers are not changing young children's diapers promptly which could pose a risk of young children obtaining a diaper rash.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Steps- Prompt (26 TAC §746.3501(1))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: A group of children between 18 to 24 months were egaging in screen time.  The caregiver corrected the deficiency during the inspection by terminating screen time and transitioning the children to music time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A caregiver without an active background check on file was in charge of a group of children.  The deficiency was corrected during this inspection when the caregiver left the premises.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: A caregiver did not wash a young child's hands with soap and running water after a diaper change.  The caregiver corrected the standard during the inspection by washing the child's hands wiith soap and running water.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child: A caregiver did not wash their hands with soap and running water after changing a child's diaper.  The caregiver corrected the deficiency during the inspection by washing their hands with soap and running water.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child (26 TAC §746.3415(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: Based on the video provided, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the standard evaluated in regard to a standard investigation.  The video confirmed a caregiver grabbing and pulling children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on interviews with collaterals, the operation was not in compliance with the standard.  Parents were not notified immediately of a situation that placed children. Management notified parents more than three days from date of the occurrence.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: Based on the video provided, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the standard evaluated in regard to a standard investigation.  The video audio confirmed a caregiver speaking in a stern loud voice.  A caregiver confirmed that the primary spoke to children in a loud stern voice could be interpreted as yelling.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on interviews with collaterals and staff, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the standard evaluated.  Management did not report to Child Care Regulations an incident that placed children at risk within the required timeframes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on the interviews with staff, the parent, and the video, the operation was found not to be in compliance with the standard evaluated.  A child was left alone in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: This standard was found to be deficient after a child was left unsupervised for approximately 20 minutes due to a caregiver's failure to conduct a required name-to-face check during a class transition. The three-year-old was found by his caregiver and the caregiver acknowledged failing to perform a thorough name-to-face roll call.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: This standard was found to be deficient as the operation had more that one classroom with cleaning liquids being accessible to the children in care. This was correct during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: This standard was found to be deficient during the investigation as the caregivers admitted to not conducting thorough name to face roll call which resulted in a child being left alone and unsupervised in a classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: This standard was found to be deficient during the investigation as there is recorded video footage that shows the caregiver forcefully grabbing the child by their ankles.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)
